gloss: to buy more of; to top up a supply

definitions.gloss: to buy more of something one already has; to top up
definitions.explanation: To make an additional purchase because the amount on hand is not enough. Implies the item is already owned or already bought once, and the new purchase supplements it.

examples.japanese: {牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}を{買|か}い{足|た}した。
{足|た}りなければ{後|あと}で{買|か}い{足|た}せばいい。
examples.english: If it isn't enough, we can just buy more later.

examples.japanese: {人数|にんずう}が{増|ふ}えたので、{飲|の}み{物|もの}とお{皿|さら}を{買|か}い{足|た}してきます。
examples.english: Since more people are coming, I'll go buy some extra drinks and plates.

notes:
Composed of {買|か}う (to buy) + {足|た}す (to add). Transitive: the item bought takes を.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive, taking を for the item added ({調味料|ちょうみりょう}を{買|か}い{足|た}す). There is no intransitive counterpart.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {足|た}りない{分|ぶん}を{買|か}い{足|た}す: to buy the amount that's short
- {後|あと}で{買|か}い{足|た}す: to buy more later
- {少|すこ}しずつ{買|か}い{足|た}す: to add to one's stock little by little

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {買|か}い{置|お}きする: to keep a stock of — buying ahead of need rather than after running short
- {買|か}い{増|ま}す: to buy more — mostly financial, as in buying more shares
- {補充|ほじゅう}する: to replenish — more formal, often about stock or supplies at work
